body.cap: Fibocom exhibit at KES 2026 | Photo - Fibocom

body.x: Getting a cellular module into a new national market takes more than a finished product. It needs local certification, network acceptance from an operator and then adoption in a customer's product before it can ship in volume.

Fibocom Wireless Inc (Stock Code: 300638.SZ; 0638.HK), a provider of AIoT solutions and wireless communication modules represented by Peter Zhang, exhibited at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. The company showed its latest 5G broadband, IoT, smart module and AI-powered solutions. Through the show, it aimed to strengthen collaboration with Korean operators, device makers and technology partners, and to accelerate product deployment and commercialization in Korea and beyond.

In Korea, Fibocom's LTE Cat.1 bis module LE270-KR has obtained KC certification and completed network acceptance with KT. The module is in mass production and has been adopted in a smart metering project. Fibocom's FG550 5G module has been deployed in FWA products from HUMAX Networks and is in mass production for an operator project in Southeast Asia. The company describes both as progress from product development and certification to commercial deployment.

The exhibits included 5G FWA modules and reference designs for CPE, MiFi and ODU applications, including the FG390. Fibocom also exhibited the LE270-KR, 5G RedCap solutions, smart modules and MagiCore, its AI companion solution.

Fibocom was founded in 1999 and is China's first wireless communication module company listed on both the A-share and H-share markets. It uses wireless communication and AI as its core technologies to provide integrated hardware and software solutions, moving industries from "Connect Everything" to "Intelligent Connectivity."

Its one-stop offering spans cellular communication, AI, automotive and GNSS modules, and AI toolchains that support integration with industry-side and mainstream large models. It also provides AI Agent, global connectivity and cloud services. These solutions serve industries including robotics, consumer electronics, the low-altitude economy, intelligent transportation, smart retail and smart energy.

Fibocom plans to keep strengthening local technical support and to work closely with Korean partners to accelerate product development, certification and commercial deployment. It will also continue expanding its portfolio from wireless connectivity toward device-level intelligence, covering 5G broadband, IoT, smart modules and AI-powered solutions, and widen commercial deployment across broadband, IoT and smart-device applications.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
